title: bug: qa_reject's soft and hard caps test the monotonic reopenCount, which non-QA reopens also bump (set_task_status, a board drag, a DONE reopen), so a row a human reopened onto the cap is parked "for a human" by its next QA reject without the one architect re-plan the soft cap promises
description:
Filed by the governor from hunt #15's held items (task-928a468d, architect-1dd28c7c, msg-492975dd). Re-verified at tip f76c55f3. It waits in BACKLOG on task-e44fbbf3, which also edits qaReject.ts and defines the parked-for-human fence this row's park relies on. The governor promotes it when e44fbbf3 is DONE.

PROBLEM
The contract:
- CLAUDE.md's lifecycle paragraph and docs/SCHEMA.md:1092: qa_reject flips to PLANNING at the reopen cap.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md:2354-2372: maxReopens and exceededReopenCap.
- The ❌ row of docs/roles/governor.md: the task parks in REVIEW for a human only past the cap.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaReject.ts:190-198 states the intent: soft cap (== maxReopens) gives the architect ONE re-plan, and the hard cap (> maxReopens) parks only because "the re-plan didn't help either".
The code (:199-206) decides both tiers from newReopenCount = reopenCount + 1 alone. reopenCount is monotonic, and non-QA reopens also bump it: set_task_status REVIEW/DONE → WORKING, the board's drag and REOPEN_TASK. So when a human reopen lands the count on maxReopens, the next QA reject reaches the hard cap directly. The row is parked for a human as "re-plan exhausted", although it never entered PLANNING.

EVIDENCE
Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/A/hardCapSkipsReplan.test.ts, run at d5431577 in a snapshot; output in hardCapSkipsReplan.vitest.txt. Both cases fail with status REVIEW (parked) where PLANNING (one re-plan) was expected:
(1) A human REVIEW → WORKING reopen at reopenCount 2, then the next QA reject.
(2) A human DONE → WORKING reopen of a row with 2 past rejects; its first new QA reject parks it.

FIX DIRECTION
Make the hard cap require that the cap re-plan actually happened. Options: record when the soft cap flips the row to PLANNING (a flag or timestamp on the task) and park only on a later reject; or count QA rejections separately from reopenCount. Error handling unchanged. Keep the audit trail (rejectionHistory, failedDodItems) as is. Rows already parked stay parked: they need no migration, and the epic rail requires backward-compatible state files, so a missing new field reads as "no re-plan yet". Sync qa_reject's MCP_SERVER.md section with the rule as shipped (ruling msg-71db57ac).

FILES
packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaReject.ts, possibly types/schema.ts if a field is added, one vitest file, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md (qa_reject section). Gate: the vitest file plus qaReject.test.ts, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout (global rail).
definitionOfDone: A row whose reopenCount reached the cap through a non-QA reopen gets ONE architect re-plan (PLANNING) on its next QA reject, not a park. Both hunt repro cases pass.
A row that already had its cap re-plan and is rejected again is still parked in REVIEW for a human. The existing qaReject.test.ts escalation cases still pass unchanged.
A legacy row without any new field behaves as "no cap re-plan yet". qa_reject's MCP_SERVER.md section states the rule.

Leave untouched: the tool description (:22), handoffWorkerId (:151) and the touchWorker call (:391-393), which task-fefce964 edits; every message, activity reason and the reply shape; rejectionHistory, failedDodItems and metrics. Error handling stays as is: no new throw, every existing refusal keeps its order and code, and a hand-edited non-string or empty value reads as absent. No load backfill, migration or schemaVersion bump (epic rail: legacy state files stay valid).

Architect ruling on a conflict between DoD 2 and DoD 3, measured at d1062cb0. It is also recorded in executionContract.compatibility.

DoD 2 asks the existing qaReject.test.ts escalation cases to pass unchanged. But 8 existing tests seed a row at reopenCount 3 or 5 that has no record of a re-plan, and they expect a park:
- 3 in qaReject.test.ts, the fixtures at :150, :159 and :180;
- 5 in parkedReview.guard.test.ts, through park().
Under DoD 3, a row without the new field reads as "no cap re-plan yet", so with the fix these rows re-plan.

The plan resolves it this way: those fixtures gain `capReplanAt`, so each models "a row that already had its cap re-plan" (DoD 2's first sentence). Every assertion stays byte-identical.

The records also pass at base. Base source plus the new tests gives 29 tests with 5 failed, and those 5 are exactly the new cases. With the fix, the full daemon suite is green: 280 files, 7439 passed.

The rejected alternative was to keep the old count rule for rows without the field. It breaks DoD 1 and DoD 3 for rows with no rejection history.

Prototype and logs: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/task-77e54ebb/.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.qa_reject parks a REVIEW task for a human only after the task's one cap re-plan has actually happened. That is the hard cap: status stays REVIEW, the task is unassigned and needsHumanReview is set. A rejection that takes reopenCount to maxReopens or beyond, on a task with no recorded cap re-plan, flips it to PLANNING (the soft cap). The same write stamps task.capReplanAt with the rejection's ISO time. A later rejection past the cap (reopenCount ≥ maxReopens + 1) on a task with capReplanAt set parks it. Non-QA reopens still bump reopenCount: set_task_status REVIEW/DONE/ARCHIVED → active work, a board drag and REOPEN_TASK. They can no longer make a task skip its re-plan. Same-DoD-item flips below the cap, WORKING rejects and parks never write capReplanAt, and nothing clears it. Error handling, the reply shape, rejectionHistory, failedDodItems and metrics are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Hunt task-928a468d's two repro cases, ported into qaReject.test.ts: a human REVIEW → WORKING or DONE → WORKING reopen lands reopenCount on 3, and the next QA reject ends in PLANNING with parkedForHuman false and needsHumanReview unset (DoD 1).

After that cap re-plan, the next QA reject parks the task. It ends in REVIEW with assignedWorkerId null, needsHumanReview true and parkedForHuman true, and capReplanAt keeps its original value. The stamp survives a StateManager reload (DoD 2).
A field-less row at reopenCount ≥ maxReopens gets PLANNING and the stamp on its next reject (DoD 3).
docs/MCP_SERVER.md's ### moe.qa_reject section states the rule: the re-plan gate, capReplanAt, non-QA reopens and the legacy reading (DoD 3).
The checkRef exits 0. It covers the full daemon suite, type-checks both test files and finds ≥ 29 tests in qaReject.test.ts.
invariants: Bounded: once capReplanAt is set, every QA reject with reopenCount ≥ maxReopens + 1 parks. A raised task.maxReopens grants one new re-plan, only when the count reaches the new cap.
capReplanAt is written only by qa_reject's soft-cap flip, in the same updateTask as status PLANNING. Nothing clears it: util/reopen.ts, setTaskStatus.ts and WebSocketServer.ts are untouched.
The park keeps routing, steps and the existing stamp. The needsHumanReview refusal still runs before any write.
rejectionHistory, failedDodItems, metrics and the reopenCount bookkeeping are unchanged.
compatibility: Legacy state: a missing, non-string or empty capReplanAt reads as 'no cap re-plan yet'. There is no migration, load backfill or schemaVersion bump (epic rail). Accepted consequence: a legacy row that already had an old-style soft-cap re-plan gets one more re-plan at its next reject past the cap, then stamps and parks as normal. Rows already parked stay parked: the needsHumanReview fence from a5157059 is unchanged.

MCP contract: qa_reject's arguments and its reply keys and their meanings are unchanged (status, parkedForHuman, needsHumanReview, exceededReopenCap, message, nextAction). capReplanAt is an additive optional task field (epic rail: no breaking change).

DoD 2 vs DoD 3, architect ruling, measured on a prototype at d1062cb0. 8 existing tests seed a field-less row at reopenCount 3 or 5 and expect a park: in qaReject.test.ts, 'sets an unset tier…; a parked task keeps its tier', 'parks in REVIEW for a human past the hard cap…' and 'does not re-flip on repeated rejects past the hard cap'; in parkedReview.guard.test.ts, 5 tests through park(). planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Count QA rejections separately (metrics.rejectCount or a new counter). Rejected: a row that reaches the cap only through human reopens would get WORKING, not the PLANNING re-plan DoD 1 names. It also changes the documented reopen-cap contract.
2. Infer the re-plan from planningEntry or rejectionHistory. Rejected: planningEntry is stamped on every PLANNING entry, history entries do not record their destination, and the description says to keep the audit trail as is.
3. A legacy fallback that keeps the 8 seeded tests literally unchanged (field-less rows keep the old count rule). Rejected: it contradicts DoD 1 and DoD 3 for history-less rows.
4. Clear capReplanAt in buildReopenClearingUpdates, for a fresh budget on a human reopen. Rejected: out of scope, and DoD 2 wants a row that had its re-plan to park on its next reject; today's code parks there too.
5. Add capReplanAt to the /ws UPDATE_TASK denylist. Rejected: the sibling latches needsHumanReview and critiqueBlockCount are not denylisted, no board client knows the key, and it would add a 6th file.
6. A new test file. Rejected: 6 distinct files floor planSizeFloor to heavy (routing.ts:156-158: more than warnDistinctFiles 5).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Prototype at d1062cb0, scratch clone, full daemon suite:
- Source change only: exactly 8 failures. 3 in qaReject.test.ts (fixtures seeded at rc 3/5) and 5 in parkedReview.guard.test.ts through park(), which seeds rc 3. The other 7434 tests pass.
- With the fixture records and the 5 new cases: 280 files, 7439 passed, pin ok, through the exact checkRef (909 chars).
- Base source plus the new tests: 29 tests | 5 failed. Only the new cases fail; the fixture records pass at base too.

Why the new key is safe:
- taskStore.updateTask merges ordinary caller keys, so the stamp persists through the normal updatePayload.
- StateManager.load backfills nothing for it, and the key survives a restart (case 3 reloads).
- buildReopenClearingUpdates clears needsHumanReview on every non-QA reopen, which is why a human un-park works. It must not clear capReplanAt.

The hunt repro's message check matches: 'Task task-1 rejected and flipped to PLANNING (reopen cap reached)…'.
